summary.en: A society of the dry river valleys of Peru’s south coast, famous for polychrome pottery, underground aqueducts (puquios) and the geoglyphs of the Nazca pampa. Its pilgrimage centre was the adobe mound complex of Cahuachi.
summary.zh: 秘鲁南部海岸干旱河谷中的社会，以多彩陶器、地下引水渠（puquio）和纳斯卡荒原上的地画闻名，其朝圣中心是卡瓦奇的土坯台丘群。

sources.title: Helaine Silverman & Donald A. Proulx, The Nasca (Blackwell, 2002)
UNESCO World Heritage: Lines and Geoglyphs of Nasca and Palpa

note: Archaeological culture; dates are approximate (c. 100 BCE – 750 CE). No ruler names survive.

capital.en: Huacas de Moche (Huaca del Sol and Huaca de la Luna)
capital.zh: 莫切神庙群（太阳神庙与月亮神庙）

summary.en: A set of warrior-priest lordships on Peru’s north coast whose craftsmen produced realistic portrait vessels and some of the finest metalwork of the ancient Americas. Rich burials at Sipán and El Brujo reveal its rulers, both men and women.
summary.zh: 秘鲁北部海岸由武士祭司统治的若干政体，工匠制作写实的肖像陶器和古代美洲最精美的金属器。西潘和埃尔布鲁霍的豪华墓葬揭示了其男女统治者。

sources.title: Walter Alva & Christopher B. Donnan, Royal Tombs of Sipán (UCLA Fowler Museum, 1993)

note: Archaeological culture of several polities; ruler years are approximate burial dates, not reigns.

capital.zh: 马兰加与普克利亚纳（里马克河谷）

summary.en: A coastal society of the Chillón, Rímac and Lurín valleys that built stepped adobe platforms such as Huaca Pucllana and early phases of Pachacamac, irrigating the desert where modern Lima now stands.
summary.zh: 分布于钦永、里马克和卢林河谷的海岸社会，修建了普克利亚纳神庙等阶梯状土坯平台以及帕查卡马克的早期建筑，在今日利马所在的荒漠上开渠灌溉。

sources.title: Isabel Flores Espinoza, Pucllana: esplendor de la cultura Lima (Instituto Cultural Peruano Norteamericano, 2005)

summary.en: An Andean state centred near the southern shore of Lake Titicaca. Its capital of carved andesite and sandstone temples fed itself with raised-field farming and llama caravans and projected influence to the Pacific coast and the Bolivian lowlands.
summary.zh: 以的的喀喀湖南岸附近为中心的安第斯国家。其首都以雕刻精美的安山岩和砂岩神庙著称，依靠台田农业和驼队贸易供养人口，影响远及太平洋沿岸与玻利维亚低地。

sources.title: Alan L. Kolata, The Tiwanaku: Portrait of an Andean Civilization (Blackwell, 1993)
UNESCO World Heritage: Tiwanaku: Spiritual and Political Centre of the Tiwanaku Culture

note: The city was occupied from the early centuries CE; its period as a regional state is usually put at c. 500–1000.

summary.en: The first Andean state to rule a long stretch of the highlands through planned administrative centres such as Pikillacta and Viracochapampa, linked by roads that the Inca later reused. Its capital near Ayacucho may have held tens of thousands of people.
summary.zh: 第一个通过皮基利亚克塔、维拉科查潘帕等规划行政中心统治大片安第斯高地的国家，其道路后来为印加人沿用。阿亚库乔附近的首都人口或达数万。

sources.title: Justin Jennings (ed.), Beyond Wari Walls: Regional Perspectives on Middle Horizon Peru (University of New Mexico Press, 2010)
William H. Isbell & Gordon F. McEwan (eds.), Huari Administrative Structure (Dumbarton Oaks, 1991)

note: Archaeological state; dates approximate (Middle Horizon, c. 600–1000).

summary.en: A north-coast society between the Moche and the Chimú, centred on the pyramids of Batán Grande. Its smiths mass-produced arsenical bronze and gold, and the Naylamp legend recorded by the Spanish preserves its dynastic memory.
summary.zh: 介于莫切与奇穆之间的北部海岸社会，以巴坦格兰德金字塔群为中心。其工匠大规模生产砷青铜和金器，西班牙人记录的纳伊兰普传说保存了其王朝记忆。

sources.title: Izumi Shimada, Cultura Sicán: Dios, riqueza y poder en la costa norte del Perú (Banco Continental, 1995)

note: Archaeological culture; Chimor conquered the Lambayeque valley around 1375.

summary.en: A people of the cloud forests on the eastern slopes of the northern Peruvian Andes, known as the “warriors of the clouds”. They built walled hilltop towns of round stone houses, cliff tombs and sarcophagi, and resisted the Inca before being conquered in the late 15th century.
summary.zh: 生活在秘鲁北部安第斯山东坡云雾林中的民族，被称为“云中武士”。他们修建了由圆形石屋组成的山顶城寨、崖墓和人形石棺，曾抵抗印加，15世纪末被征服。

sources.title: Warren B. Church & Adriana von Hagen, “Chachapoyas: Cultural Development at an Andean Cloud Forest Crossroads”, in H. Silverman & W. Isbell (eds.), Handbook of South American Archaeology (Springer, 2008)

note: Dates approximate; Kuélap itself was begun several centuries earlier.

summary.en: The largest coastal kingdom of the Andes before the Inca, stretching about 1,000 km along Peru’s north coast at its height. Its kings ruled from walled palace compounds at Chan Chan and controlled irrigation canals linking whole valleys, until Topa Inca conquered it around 1470.
summary.zh: 印加之前安第斯最大的海岸王国，鼎盛时沿秘鲁北部海岸延伸约1000公里。国王居于昌昌的围墙宫殿院落，掌握连通多个河谷的灌溉渠系，约1470年为图帕克·印卡所灭。

name.zh: 泰卡纳莫（传说中的开国者）

sources.title: Michael E. Moseley & Alana Cordy-Collins (eds.), The Northern Dynasties: Kingship and Statecraft in Chimor (Dumbarton Oaks, 1990)
UNESCO World Heritage: Chan Chan Archaeological Zone

note: King list survives only in the anonymous Historia anónima de Trujillo (1604); Taycanamo is legendary and his dates are conventional.

summary.en: Chiefdoms of Colombia’s Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta that built stone-paved towns of terraces, stairways and house platforms and worked gold in a distinctive cast style. They resisted Spanish rule until the revolts of the late 16th century; the Kogi, Arhuaco and Wiwa are their descendants.
summary.zh: 哥伦比亚圣玛尔塔内华达山脉中的酋邦，修建了由梯田、石阶和屋基构成的石铺城镇，并以独特的铸造工艺制作金器。他们抵抗西班牙统治直至16世纪末的起义失败；今天的科吉人、阿瓦科人和维瓦人是其后裔。

sources.title: ICANH, Parque Arqueológico Teyuna – Ciudad Perdida

note: Dates approximate; Tairona-period towns flourished c. 900–1600.

capital.zh: 巴卡塔（丰萨）与洪萨（通哈）

summary.en: The Chibcha-speaking Muisca of Colombia’s eastern highlands were organised into rival confederations under the zipa of Bacatá and the zaque of Hunza. They traded salt, emeralds and cotton cloth, and their gold offerings at sacred lakes gave rise to the legend of El Dorado.
summary.zh: 哥伦比亚东部高原讲奇布查语的穆伊斯卡人分属巴卡塔的“西帕”与洪萨的“萨克”统领的两大联盟。他们贸易盐、祖母绿和棉布，在圣湖投献金器的习俗催生了“黄金国”传说。

sources.title: Carl Henrik Langebaek, Los muiscas: la historia milenaria de un pueblo chibcha (Debate, 2019)

note: Muisca culture dates from c. 600–800 CE; the confederations took shape in the 15th century. Reign dates of zipas and zaques come from colonial chronicles and are approximate.

summary.en: The small highland kingdom from which the Inca Empire grew. Inca tradition lists eight rulers from the legendary founder Manco Capac to Viracocha Inca before Pachacuti’s victory over the Chanka transformed it into an empire.
summary.zh: 印加帝国兴起前的高原小王国。印加传统列出从传说中的开国者曼科·卡帕克到维拉科查·印卡共八位君主，直到帕查库蒂战胜昌卡人，王国才转变为帝国。

sources.title: Brian S. Bauer, The Development of the Inca State (University of Texas Press, 1992)
Juan de Betanzos, Suma y narración de los Incas (1551)

note: Reign dates before Pachacuti are conventional estimates; the early rulers are known only from oral tradition recorded after the conquest.

summary.en: Tawantinsuyu, “the four parts together”, was the largest state of the pre-Columbian Americas, stretching from southern Colombia to central Chile. It ran without markets or writing, using labour tribute, state storehouses, khipu records and some 40,000 km of roads.
summary.zh: 塔万廷苏尤意为“四方合一”，是前哥伦布时期美洲最大的国家，疆域从哥伦比亚南部延伸至智利中部。它没有市场和文字，依靠劳役赋税、国家仓储、结绳记事（基普）和约四万公里道路运转。

sources.title: Terence N. D’Altroy, The Incas (2nd ed., Wiley-Blackwell, 2015)

note: The 1438 start and Pachacuti’s reign follow the chronology of John Rowe (from Cabello Valboa); some scholars prefer an earlier, more gradual expansion.

summary.en: After the failed siege of Cusco, Manco Inca withdrew into the rugged Vilcabamba region and ruled an independent Inca kingdom there for 35 years. It ended when Viceroy Toledo’s troops captured the last Sapa Inca, Túpac Amaru, in 1572.
summary.zh: 围攻库斯科失败后，曼科·印卡退入崎岖的比尔卡班巴地区，在那里维持了一个独立的印加王国达35年。1572年总督托莱多的军队俘获最后一位萨帕印卡图帕克·阿马鲁，该国灭亡。

sources.title: John Hemming, The Conquest of the Incas (Macmillan, 1970)
Titu Cusi Yupanqui, Instrucción del Inga don Diego de Castro Titu Cusi Yupangui (1570)

summary.en: Created by the New Laws of 1542, the viceroyalty governed most of Spanish South America from Lima for two centuries. The silver of Potosí made it the richest part of the empire; it shrank after New Granada and Río de la Plata were split off and ended with the defeat at Ayacucho.
summary.zh: 依据1542年《新法》设立，在两个世纪里以利马为中心管辖西属南美的大部分地区。波托西白银使其成为帝国最富庶的部分；新格拉纳达和拉普拉塔分立后疆域缩小，最终随阿亚库乔战败而终结。

name.en: Francisco de Borja y Aragón, Prince of Esquilache
name.zh: 埃斯基拉切亲王弗朗西斯科·德·博尔哈
何塞·安东尼奥·曼索·德·贝拉斯科
何塞·费尔南多·德·阿瓦斯卡尔

sources.title: Kenneth J. Andrien, Andean Worlds: Indigenous History, Culture and Consciousness under Spanish Rule, 1532–1825 (University of New Mexico Press, 2001)

summary.en: Spanish Chile, founded by Pedro de Valdivia, was a poor, embattled frontier province under the Viceroyalty of Peru. Its governors spent much of their resources on the Arauco War against the Mapuche, whose lands south of the Biobío stayed independent.
summary.zh: 由佩德罗·德·瓦尔迪维亚开拓的西属智利是秘鲁总督区下一个贫穷而多战的边疆省份。历任总督将大量资源投入对马普切人的阿劳科战争，比奥比奥河以南的马普切土地始终保持独立。

name.zh: 加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨
何塞·安东尼奥·曼索·德·贝拉斯科
马特奥·德·托罗·桑布拉诺

sources.title: Simon Collier & William F. Sater, A History of Chile, 1808–2002 (Cambridge UP, 2004)
Diego Barros Arana, Historia general de Chile (1884–1902)

summary.en: Portugal’s American colony grew from coastal captaincies into the world’s leading sugar producer and, after 1693, a great gold economy, both worked by millions of enslaved Africans. The royal court’s arrival in 1808 and elevation to a kingdom in 1815 prepared independence in 1822.
summary.zh: 葡萄牙的美洲殖民地由沿海受封领地发展为世界最大的产糖地，1693年后又成为重要的产金区，两者都依靠数百万被奴役的非洲人劳作。1808年王室迁来、1815年升格为王国，为1822年独立铺平了道路。

name.en: Antônio Álvares da Cunha (first viceroy at Rio)
name.zh: 安东尼奥·阿尔瓦雷斯·达·库尼亚（首任驻里约副王）

name.en: John VI (prince regent, then king, in Rio)
name.zh: 若昂六世（在里约任摄政王及国王）

sources.title: Boris Fausto, A Concise History of Brazil (Cambridge UP, 1999)
Stuart B. Schwartz, Sugar Plantations in the Formation of Brazilian Society: Bahia, 1550–1835 (Cambridge UP, 1985)

note: From 1815 Brazil was a kingdom within the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves; this record runs to independence in 1822.

capital.zh: 累西腓 / 毛里茨斯塔德

summary.en: The Dutch West India Company seized Pernambuco, Brazil’s richest sugar captaincy, in 1630. Under Johan Maurits of Nassau-Siegen it became a cosmopolitan colony of scientists, painters and a Jewish community, before Luso-Brazilian rebels expelled the Dutch in 1654.
summary.zh: 荷兰西印度公司于1630年夺取巴西最富庶的产糖领地伯南布哥。在拿骚-锡根的约翰·毛里茨治下，这里成为汇聚科学家、画家和犹太社群的国际化殖民地，1654年被葡裔巴西起义者驱逐。

name.zh: 拿骚-锡根的约翰·毛里茨

sources.title: C. R. Boxer, The Dutch in Brazil, 1624–1654 (Clarendon Press, 1957)

summary.en: Carved out of Peru to defend the Caribbean coast and control contraband, the viceroyalty covered today’s Colombia, Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela. It was briefly abolished in 1723, restored in 1739, and collapsed after Bolívar’s victory at Boyacá.
summary.zh: 为防卫加勒比海岸、遏制走私而从秘鲁分设，辖今哥伦比亚、厄瓜多尔、巴拿马和委内瑞拉。1723年一度撤销，1739年恢复，玻利瓦尔在博亚卡获胜后瓦解。

name.zh: 塞巴斯蒂安·德·埃斯拉瓦
佩德罗·梅西亚·德拉塞尔达
安东尼奥·卡瓦列罗-贡戈拉

sources.title: Anthony McFarlane, Colombia before Independence: Economy, Society and Politics under Bourbon Rule (Cambridge UP, 1993)

note: Suspended 1723–1739. Royalist forces held parts of the territory until 1822.

name.en: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata

summary.en: Created in 1776 to block Portuguese expansion and to route Potosí’s silver through Buenos Aires rather than Lima, it joined today’s Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay. The May Revolution of 1810 deposed its last viceroy; royalist Montevideo fell in 1814.
summary.zh: 1776年设立，旨在遏制葡萄牙扩张，并让波托西白银经布宜诺斯艾利斯而非利马外运，辖今阿根廷、玻利维亚、巴拉圭和乌拉圭。1810年五月革命废黜末任总督，保王派据守的蒙得维的亚于1814年陷落。

name.en: Juan José de Vértiz y Salcedo

name.zh: 圣地亚哥·德·利尼耶尔斯
巴尔塔萨尔·伊达尔戈·德·西斯内罗斯

sources.title: Wikipedia: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
John Lynch, Spanish Colonial Administration, 1782–1810: The Intendant System in the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata (Athlone, 1958)

summary.en: Paraguay broke from Buenos Aires and Spain in 1811 and was sealed off from the world by the dictator Francia. Under the Lópezes it built a strong state and army, then lost much of its population in the Paraguayan War (1864–70); the Stroessner dictatorship lasted from 1954 to 1989.
summary.zh: 巴拉圭于1811年脱离布宜诺斯艾利斯与西班牙，独裁者弗朗西亚使其与外界隔绝。洛佩斯父子时期建立起强大的国家和军队，随后在巴拉圭战争（1864–1870）中损失大量人口；斯特罗斯纳独裁统治持续于1954至1989年。

name.zh: 何塞·加斯帕尔·罗德里格斯·德·弗朗西亚
卡洛斯·安东尼奥·洛佩斯
弗朗西斯科·索拉诺·洛佩斯
阿尔弗雷多·斯特罗斯纳

sources.title: Thomas L. Whigham, The Paraguayan War, vol. 1 (University of Nebraska Press, 2002)

summary.en: The United Provinces of the Río de la Plata declared independence at Tucumán in 1816. After decades of civil war between Buenos Aires and the provinces, a federal republic took shape in 1853–80 and grew rich on grain, beef and European immigration; the 20th century brought Peronism, coups and, from 1983, democracy.
summary.zh: 拉普拉塔联合省于1816年在图库曼宣布独立。经过布宜诺斯艾利斯与各省之间数十年内战，联邦共和国在1853至1880年间成形，并凭借谷物、牛肉和欧洲移民致富；20世纪经历了庇隆主义、多次政变，1983年起恢复民主。

name.zh: 胡安·曼努埃尔·德·罗萨斯
多明戈·福斯蒂诺·萨米恩托

sources.title: David Rock, Argentina 1516–1987 (University of California Press, 1987)

note: Rosas was governor of Buenos Aires Province, exercising the Confederation’s foreign affairs.

summary.en: Independent from 1818, Chile became one of Latin America’s most stable 19th-century republics, won the nitrate provinces in the War of the Pacific and conquered Araucanía. In 1973 a military coup overthrew Salvador Allende; democracy returned in 1990.
summary.zh: 智利自1818年独立，是19世纪拉丁美洲最稳定的共和国之一，在太平洋战争中夺得硝石产区并征服阿劳卡尼亚。1973年军事政变推翻萨尔瓦多·阿连德，1990年恢复民主。

name.zh: 何塞·曼努埃尔·巴尔马塞达

sources.title: Simon Collier & William F. Sater, A History of Chile, 1808–2002 (Cambridge UP, 2004)

summary.en: Bolívar’s Republic of Colombia, proclaimed at Angostura in 1819 and organised at Cúcuta in 1821, united today’s Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama. Regional rivalries tore it apart: Venezuela and Ecuador seceded in 1830, the year Bolívar died.
summary.zh: 玻利瓦尔的哥伦比亚共和国于1819年在安戈斯图拉宣告成立，1821年在库库塔制定宪法，统合今哥伦比亚、委内瑞拉、厄瓜多尔和巴拿马。地区矛盾使其分裂：1830年委内瑞拉与厄瓜多尔脱离，同年玻利瓦尔去世。

name.zh: 弗朗西斯科·德保拉·桑坦德（代总统）

sources.title: David Bushnell, The Santander Regime in Gran Colombia (University of Delaware Press, 1954)
John Lynch, Simón Bolívar: A Life (Yale UP, 2006)

summary.en: San Martín proclaimed Peru’s independence in Lima in 1821, but royalist armies held the highlands until Ayacucho in 1824. The guano boom of the mid-19th century funded railways and the abolition of slavery; defeat by Chile in 1879–83 cost the nitrate south.
summary.zh: 1821年圣马丁在利马宣布秘鲁独立，但保王军一直据守高原，直到1824年阿亚库乔战役。19世纪中叶的鸟粪繁荣为修建铁路和废除奴隶制提供了资金；1879至1883年败于智利，失去南部硝石产区。

name.zh: 胡安·贝拉斯科·阿尔瓦拉多

sources.title: Peter F. Klarén, Peru: Society and Nationhood in the Andes (Oxford UP, 2000)

summary.en: Brazil became independent as a constitutional monarchy under the Braganza heir Pedro I, which kept the vast territory united while Spanish America splintered. Coffee and slavery underpinned the empire; abolition in 1888 cost it the planters’ support and a military coup ended it in 1889.
summary.zh: 巴西以布拉干萨王朝继承人佩德罗一世为君主，作为君主立宪国独立，在西属美洲分裂之际保持了辽阔疆土的统一。咖啡与奴隶制是帝国的支柱；1888年废奴使其失去种植园主支持，1889年军事政变终结了帝制。

name.zh: 迪奥戈·安东尼奥·费若（摄政）

sources.title: Roderick J. Barman, Brazil: The Forging of a Nation, 1798–1852 (Stanford UP, 1988)
Roderick J. Barman, Citizen Emperor: Pedro II and the Making of Brazil, 1825–91 (Stanford UP, 1999)

note: Pedro II succeeded in 1831 as a child; regents governed until he was declared of age in 1840.

capital.zh: 苏克雷（宪法首都）、拉巴斯（政府所在地）

summary.en: Upper Peru became independent in 1825 and named itself after Bolívar. It lost its Pacific coast to Chile in 1879–84 and the Chaco to Paraguay in 1932–35; the 1952 revolution nationalised the tin mines, and in 2006 Evo Morales became its first Indigenous president.
summary.zh: 上秘鲁于1825年独立，以玻利瓦尔之名命名国家。1879至1884年将太平洋海岸输给智利，1932至1935年失去查科地区；1952年革命将锡矿收归国有，2006年埃沃·莫拉莱斯成为首位原住民总统。

name.zh: 安东尼奥·何塞·德·苏克雷
维克托·帕斯·埃斯登索罗

sources.title: Herbert S. Klein, A Concise History of Bolivia (Cambridge UP, 2003)

summary.en: The Banda Oriental, fought over by Spain, Portugal, Brazil and Buenos Aires, became independent as a buffer state under British mediation in 1828. Under José Batlle y Ordóñez in the early 20th century it built one of the world’s first welfare states.
summary.zh: 东岸地区曾被西班牙、葡萄牙、巴西和布宜诺斯艾利斯反复争夺，1828年在英国调停下作为缓冲国独立。20世纪初在何塞·巴特列-奥多涅斯领导下建立了世界上最早的福利国家之一。

sources.title: Lindsay Lyons, Uruguay: A History (Oxford UP, 2002)

summary.en: Venezuela left Gran Colombia in 1830 under the llanero general José Antonio Páez. A century of caudillo rule ended in oil wealth under Juan Vicente Gómez; democracy from 1958 gave way to Hugo Chávez’s Bolivarian Revolution in 1999.
summary.zh: 1830年在平原将军何塞·安东尼奥·派斯领导下脱离大哥伦比亚。一个世纪的考迪罗统治在胡安·维森特·戈麦斯时期迎来石油财富；1958年起的民主体制后由1999年乌戈·查韦斯的“玻利瓦尔革命”取代。

name.zh: 安东尼奥·古斯曼·布兰科

sources.title: John V. Lombardi, Venezuela: The Search for Order, the Dream of Progress (Oxford UP, 1982)

summary.en: Ecuador seceded from Gran Colombia in 1830 under the Venezuelan general Juan José Flores. Its politics long pitted conservative Quito against liberal, export-oriented Guayaquil, from the Catholic state of García Moreno to Eloy Alfaro’s Liberal Revolution of 1895.
summary.zh: 1830年在委内瑞拉籍将军胡安·何塞·弗洛雷斯领导下脱离大哥伦比亚。其政治长期是保守的基多与自由、面向出口的瓜亚基尔之争，从加西亚·莫雷诺的天主教国家到1895年埃洛伊·阿尔法罗的自由主义革命。

name.zh: 加夫列尔·加西亚·莫雷诺

sources.title: Linda Alexander Rodríguez, The Search for Public Policy: Regional Politics and Government Finances in Ecuador, 1830–1940 (University of California Press, 1985)

summary.en: The core of Gran Colombia re-formed as the Republic of New Granada in 1831, became the federal United States of Colombia in 1863 and the centralised Republic of Colombia in 1886. Civil wars between Liberals and Conservatives culminated in La Violencia, and a FARC peace accord was signed in 2016.
summary.zh: 大哥伦比亚的核心地区于1831年重组为新格拉纳达共和国，1863年成为联邦制的哥伦比亚合众国，1886年改为中央集权的哥伦比亚共和国。自由党与保守党之间的内战最终演变为“暴力时期”，2016年与哥伦比亚革命武装力量签署和平协议。

name.zh: 弗朗西斯科·德保拉·桑坦德
托马斯·西普里亚诺·德·莫斯克拉
阿方索·洛佩斯·普马雷霍

sources.title: David Bushnell, The Making of Modern Colombia: A Nation in Spite of Itself (University of California Press, 1993)

name.zh: 巴西第一共和国（旧共和国）

summary.en: The army proclaimed the republic in November 1889. A federal system dominated by the coffee oligarchies of São Paulo and Minas Gerais (the “café com leite” politics) governed until the Revolution of 1930 brought Getúlio Vargas to power.
summary.zh: 1889年11月军队宣布成立共和国。由圣保罗和米纳斯吉拉斯咖啡寡头主导的联邦体制（所谓“牛奶咖啡”政治）一直延续，直到1930年革命使热图利奥·瓦加斯掌权。

sources.title: Boris Fausto, A Concise History of Brazil (Cambridge UP, 1999)
Lilia M. Schwarcz & Heloisa M. Starling, Brazil: A Biography (Allen Lane, 2018)

capital.zh: 里约热内卢（至1960年）、巴西利亚

summary.en: From the Vargas era through the democratic republic of 1946, the military regime of 1964–85 and the New Republic, Brazil industrialised, moved its capital inland to Brasília in 1960 and became the largest economy of Latin America.
summary.zh: 从瓦加斯时代、1946年的民主共和国、1964至1985年的军政府到“新共和国”，巴西实现工业化，1960年将首都内迁至巴西利亚，成为拉丁美洲最大的经济体。

name.zh: 费尔南多·恩里克·卡多佐
路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦
